title: Optimize Apply Flow — Quality Guardrails Gating UX + API Behavior Spec
author: Kenji Nakamura

Spec: Audit events for Optimize config changes (security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimize-config-change-audit-events)
body:
## Summary
This page defines the Console/UI experience and API behavior for gating any **Optimize-driven configuration apply** behind **quality guardrails**.

The spec covers:
- Where gating appears in the Optimize “Apply” flow in the Console.
- How to represent gating results (metric deltas, confidence, sample sizes, suite versions).
- What happens on **PASS**, **FAIL**, **TIMEOUT**, **EVAL ERROR**, and **PARTIAL** outcomes.
- Reruns, viewing artifacts, and the **override with justification** path.
- Enforcement modes (observe-only → soft-block → hard-block) and tier-based behavior.

Out of scope:
- Definition of the metrics themselves and threshold methodology (see Applied ML guardrails pages).
- Implementation details of the eval runner / harness.

---

## Definitions
**Optimization proposal**: A set of recommended config changes produced by Optimize (e.g., quantization profile change, batching policy adjustment, caching tweaks, routing policy changes).

**Gating run**: An evaluation run executed against a prompt set + suite selection that produces a structured “gating result” and artifact links.

**Baseline**: The currently active configuration on the target route/deployment that we compare against.

**Enforcement mode** (control plane):
- **Observe-only**: gating runs and results are recorded; apply is allowed regardless.
- **Soft-block**: apply is blocked by default, but users with override permissions can proceed.
- **Hard-block**: apply is blocked; no override in product UI (except break-glass operational path).

**Outcome state** (gating result):
- **PASS**: All required checks satisfied.
- **FAIL**: One or more required checks violated.
- **PARTIAL**: Some checks succeeded, but one or more are missing (e.g., suite subset ran; non-required checks failed; or data insufficiency).
- **TIMEOUT**: Gating did not complete within UI time budget; run may still complete asynchronously.
- **EVAL_ERROR**: Runner/harness error prevented producing a valid result.

---

## User Personas and Goals
### Primary personas
- **ML / Platform engineer** applying Optimize changes to reduce cost while maintaining quality.
- **Product engineer** applying improvements in latency/throughput who needs a clear “safe to ship” signal.
- **SRE / on-call** investigating outages/backlogs/timeouts and ensuring safe-degrade behavior.

### UX goals
1. Make it obvious whether a proposed change is safe to apply.
2. Provide actionable failure reasons (which metric, how far, confidence, sample size).
3. Make override controlled, auditable, and rare.
4. Avoid “flaky” experiences: clear status transitions, deterministic display ordering, stable identifiers.

---

## Placement in Console: Optimize Apply Flow
### Entry point
Optimize Console → Recommendation detail page → **Apply** CTA.

### Gating panel placement
During apply review, show a dedicated section above the final “Apply changes” button:
- Section title: **Quality guardrails (required)**
- Status chip: Not started / Running / Pass / Fail / Timeout / Error / Partial
- Summary row: “Suite: <suite_name> • Prompt set: <prompt_set_name>@<rev> • Model: <model>@<version>”

### Apply flow (high-level)
1. User opens recommendation.
2. User clicks **Apply**.
3. Apply modal (or page) shows:
   - “Config changes” diff
   - “Rollout strategy” (canary/gradual) selection (if available)
   - **Quality guardrails** section with latest gating status
4. If no recent gating result is eligible, user triggers gating (automatic by default; manual rerun available).
5. Based on gating + enforcement mode, “Apply changes” is allowed, blocked, or requires override.

---

## When Gating Runs (Trigger Rules)
### Automatic gating on open
By default, gating is kicked off when the user opens the Apply review screen if there is no eligible cached result.

Eligibility for cached results (UI messaging only; actual decision enforced by API):
A previous gating run may be reused if all are identical:
- target route/deployment identifier
- model identifier + model version
- baseline config hash
- proposed config delta hash
- prompt set revision
- suite definition version
- threshold policy version
- runner version (major)

UI should show if the result is cached:
- “Using cached result from <timestamp>”
- Link: “View run details”

### Manual rerun
User can click **Rerun checks** when:
- Run is PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL/TIMEOUT/ERROR
- User has permission to rerun (default: all users who can apply Optimize changes)

Rerun behavior:
- Creates a new run_id
- Does not delete previous runs
- UI shows newest run as “current” and keeps history accessible

---

## UI States and Actions
### State table
| State | Status chip | Primary text | Apply button behavior | Primary actions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not started | Not started | “Checks will run before applying changes.” | Disabled until run starts (unless observe-only + explicit ‘Skip’ flag; see rollout) | Start checks (if auto-run disabled), Learn more |
| Running | Running | “Running quality checks (ETA ~<x> min).” | Disabled | View details, Cancel apply |
| PASS | Pass | “No quality regressions detected.” | Enabled | View metrics, View artifacts, Apply |
| FAIL | Fail | “Quality regression detected. Apply is blocked.” | Disabled in hard-block; enabled only after override in soft-block | View failure reasons, Rerun, Request override |
| PARTIAL | Partial | “Checks incomplete. Review before proceeding.” | Typically Disabled; can be Enabled only in observe-only | View what’s missing, Rerun |
| TIMEOUT | Timeout | “Checks timed out. Try again or contact support.” | Disabled by default | Rerun, View runner status link, Request override (only if policy allows) |
| EVAL ERROR | Error | “Checks failed to run due to an error.” | Disabled by default | Rerun, View error details |

### Result ordering and determinism
- Metric rows must be displayed in stable sorted order:
  1) Required metrics first, then optional
  2) Within group, alphabetical by metric_key
- Suites listed in stable order (suite_id ascending).
- If multiple required suites exist, display a per-suite breakdown and an overall summary.

---

## Results Display: What the User Sees
### Summary block (always shown once run completes)
- Overall decision: PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL
- “Compared to baseline” label
- Confidence label (derived from policy rules):
  - “High confidence” when all required metrics have valid confidence intervals and minimum sample size
  - “Medium confidence” when some metrics use non-CI heuristic thresholds
  - “Low confidence” when partial or data insufficient

Include:
- Prompt set: name + revision
- Eval suite(s): name + version
- Threshold policy: policy_id + version
- Run duration + timestamp
- Links:
  - “View artifacts” (opens artifact viewer)
  - “Copy run ID”

### Metrics table (required)
Columns:
- Metric
- Baseline
- Proposed
- Δ (delta)
- Threshold
- 95% CI (if available)
- Sample size (n)
- Status (Pass/Fail/Not computed)

Notes:
- Baseline and Proposed values must include units and normalization information (e.g., “rubric_score (0–5)”, “toxicity_rate (%)”).
- Δ should use directional semantics:
  - Higher is better metrics: negative Δ is regression.
  - Lower is better metrics: positive Δ is regression.
- When CI is present, show in compact form, e.g. “[-0.04, -0.01]”.

### Failure reasons panel (shown on FAIL)
A dedicated block titled “Why this failed” that enumerates:
- Metric(s) violated
- How far beyond threshold
- Whether decision is CI-based, min-sample-based, or absolute delta-based
- Recommended next steps (generated from a small fixed playbook; not freeform model output):
  - “Rerun checks (possible flake)”,
  - “Inspect artifact examples”,
  - “Try a safer profile (recommended: <profile_name>)”,
  - “Split rollout (canary) and rerun gating”,
  - “Request override (requires justification)”.

### Artifact viewer (link out)
The UI should not attempt to render raw prompt/response pairs inline by default due to volume and potential sensitivity.
- “View artifacts” opens a separate page with filtering:
  - by suite
  - by metric
  - by tag (workload tags)
  - by outcome bucket (regression examples)
- Artifact page shows redaction banner if any content is restricted.

---

## Override UX (Soft-block Only)
### Who can override
Controlled by RBAC permissions (see Control Plane / RBAC spec). UI must check permission before presenting override CTA.

Recommended role naming (for copy only; actual role strings per RBAC service):
- “Optimize Guardrails Override” permission

### Override entry point
On FAIL/TIMEOUT/EVAL ERROR in soft-block mode, show:
- Button: **Request override**

### Override modal requirements
Fields (required unless noted):
- Justification (required, min 50 chars)
- Incident/ticket reference (optional; e.g., “INC-1234”, “SUP-18503”)
- Expiration (required; default 24 hours; max 7 days)
- Acknowledgement checkbox: “I understand this may cause a user-visible quality regression.”

Approval model
- V1: single-actor override allowed if user has permission.
- Optional future: 2-person approval for restricted tenants (out of scope but leave UI space for “pending approval”).

After override is granted:
- Apply button becomes enabled and shows “Apply (override)” styling.
- The apply confirmation screen repeats the override rationale and expiration.

Audit requirements (UI responsibilities)
- UI must pass through justification + references to the apply API.
- UI must display “This action will be audited.”

---

## Timeout and Long-Running Runs
### UI time budgets
- Target: 90 seconds to first meaningful update (Running state).
- Typical gating completion: 5–15 minutes depending on suite.

Because runs can exceed typical page dwell time, UI must support asynchronous continuation:
- If user navigates away, the run continues.
- When user returns to Apply screen, fetch latest status.

### Timeout semantics
There are two timeouts:
1) **UI timeout**: if no completion after N minutes (default 20), show TIMEOUT state.
2) **Runner timeout**: runner may terminate and return TIMEOUT/ERROR.

UI should message clearly:
- “Timed out waiting for results. The run may still be processing; check back or rerun.”

---

## Safe-Degrade UX (Runner or Policy Service Issues)
When dependencies are degraded, the API returns a deterministic outcome and the UI must reflect it.

### Degraded dependency cases
- Eval runner unavailable
- Result store unavailable
- Policy evaluation service unavailable

UI requirements
- Show a banner in the guardrails section:
  - Title: “Quality checks unavailable”
  - Body: short text, include run_id if present
  - Link to status page (internal) or “Contact support” (customer-facing)

Apply behavior is determined by enforcement mode and tenant tier:
- Hard-block: apply remains blocked.
- Soft-block: apply blocked; override may be allowed.
- Observe-only: allow apply but show warning.

---

## API: Endpoints and Contracts (Console-facing)
This section defines the UI-facing behavior; exact routing may differ between gateway vs internal services.

### 1) Start apply (or “preview apply”) with gating
**POST** `/v1/optimize/applies:prepare`
Purpose: Create an “apply intent” and ensure a gating run exists (reusing cached run if eligible).

Request (conceptual JSON; fields are illustrative):
- tenant_id
- target (route/deployment)
- recommendation_id
- proposed_config_delta
- rollout_plan (optional)

Response fields (must be stable and backward compatible):
- apply_intent_id
- gating_required (boolean)
- gating_enforcement_mode: `observe_only | soft_block | hard_block`
- gating_run_id (string; may be empty if not required)
- gating_status: `not_started | running | completed`
- gating_decision (when completed): `pass | fail | partial | timeout | error`
- gating_decision_reason_codes (comma-separated string list)
- gating_result_ref (URL or opaque ref for artifact viewer)
- next_poll_after_ms

UI behavior:
- If `gating_status=running`, start polling run status endpoint.


### 2) Poll gating run status
**GET** `/v1/guardrails/runs/{run_id}`
Purpose: Retrieve structured summary for display.

Response fields:
- run_id
- status: `running | completed`
- decision: `pass | fail | partial | timeout | error` (only when completed)
- decision_summary (short, human-readable)
- suite_ids (comma-separated)
- suite_versions (comma-separated)
- prompt_set_id, prompt_set_revision
- model_id, model_version
- baseline_config_hash
- proposed_config_hash
- policy_id, policy_version
- created_at, completed_at
- duration_ms
- metrics_table (serialized as a string blob for UI; see note below)
- artifact_links (comma-separated or newline-separated)
- error_message (only if error)

Note: Because this Confluence spec is not binding on internal serialization, the only hard requirement is that the Console can render a metrics table with:
- baseline, proposed, delta
- threshold
- CI bounds (optional)
- sample size
- per-metric pass/fail


### 3) Submit apply (finalize)
**POST** `/v1/optimize/applies`
Purpose: Perform the configuration apply (or schedule it) and enforce gating.

Request includes:
- apply_intent_id
- gating_run_id (if required)
- override (optional): justification, reference, expiration

Response fields:
- apply_id
- accepted (boolean)
- enforcement_mode
- gating_decision
- blocked_reason (if not accepted)
- rollback_hook_ref (if applicable)
- audit_event_id

Blocking behavior
- In soft/hard block, if gating decision is FAIL/PARTIAL/TIMEOUT/ERROR, API returns `accepted=false` with blocked_reason.
- In observe-only, API may return accepted=true but still returns gating_decision for visibility.


### 4) Rerun gating
**POST** `/v1/guardrails/runs`
Purpose: Create a new run for the same apply intent / proposed delta.

Response fields:
- run_id
- status=running
- next_poll_after_ms

---

## Error Handling and Copy Requirements
### Error copy guidelines
- Avoid blaming language. Prefer: “We couldn’t complete the checks” over “You did X wrong.”
- Include a stable run identifier whenever possible.
- Provide a next step (rerun, view status, contact support).

### Common blocked reasons (display strings)
UI should map API `blocked_reason` codes to customer-safe messages:
- `QUALITY_REGRESSION_DETECTED` → “Quality regression detected. This change is blocked by guardrails.”
- `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE_SIZE` → “Not enough samples to make a reliable decision. Rerun checks or expand prompt coverage.”
- `REQUIRED_SUITE_MISSING` → “Required evaluation suite did not complete. Rerun checks.”
- `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` → “Quality checks are currently unavailable. Try again later.”

---

## Rollout / Feature Flag Behavior (UI)
UI must support phased rollout without confusing users.

### Flags (conceptual)
- `guardrails_gating_ui_enabled`
- `guardrails_gating_auto_run_enabled`
- `guardrails_soft_block_enabled`
- `guardrails_hard_block_enabled`
- `guardrails_override_enabled`

### Stages
1) **Observe-only**: show results, allow apply.
2) **Soft-block**: block on fail; allow override for permitted roles.
3) **Hard-block**: block on fail; override hidden (except break-glass tooling outside Console).

UI must always reflect what the API enforces. Do not “guess” enforcement from flags alone.

---

## Accessibility and Information Density Requirements
- Status chip must have non-color indicator (icon + label).
- Metrics table must be keyboard navigable.
- Provide “Copy run ID” for support workflows.
- Default view shows summary + top failed metrics; expand for full table.

---

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A user can start an Optimize apply and see guardrails status change from Not started → Running → Completed.
2. On PASS, user sees summary + metrics table and can apply.
3. On FAIL, user sees:
   - overall FAIL
   - at least one explicit failed metric row
   - a “Why this failed” panel
   - apply is blocked in soft/hard block modes
4. On TIMEOUT, user sees TIMEOUT state and can rerun; apply remains blocked in soft/hard block modes.
5. Override path:
   - only available to permitted roles
   - requires justification
   - results in “Apply (override)” and is passed to API
6. All states expose run_id and a link to artifacts.

---

## Open Questions
1. Do we require an explicit “Run checks” click for specific tenants (regulated) or always auto-run on apply screen?
2. Should TIMEOUT be eligible for override in soft-block for enterprise tiers, or only FAIL with a completed run?
3. How should we message PARTIAL when required metrics pass but optional metrics fail (do we label as PASS with warnings vs PARTIAL)?
4. What is the default recency window for cached results (e.g., 7 days) in addition to exact-hash match?

---

## Changelog
- 2025-02-06: Added explicit PARTIAL handling and clarified timeout semantics (UI vs runner). Added override modal requirements.
- 2025-01-29: Added metrics table columns (CI + sample size) and stable sorting rules.
- 2025-01-17: Initial draft of apply flow placement and enforcement-mode mapping.
